主要内容: The article discusses Energy Transfer Equity (ETE) as a complex company due to its ownership in multiple MLPs, which complicates its structure and growth potential. It highlights that simpler midstream MLPs like Enterprise Products Partners (EPD), Magellan Midstream Partners (MMP), and Buckeye Partners (BPL) offer better strategic advantages. These companies simplified their structures by acquiring their general partners, reducing capital costs and administrative expenses. This allowed them to retain more cash for reinvestment and maintain higher distribution growth rates compared to ETE. The article also notes that these companies have issued fewer units and less debt, maintaining investment-grade credit ratings. The simplified structure provides a competitive edge over peers like Energy Transfer Partners (ETP), which still rely on general partners and face higher capital market demands. The article highlights that Energy Transfer Equity, LP (ETE) is a complex energy company due to its role as the general partner to a growing number of MLPs. This complexity makes it harder for investors to understand and has acted as a financial burden on the organization. ETE has a credit rating of BB, which is below investment grade, due to concerns over its debt. In contrast, other MLPs like Enterprise Products Partners (EPD), Magellan Midstream Partners, and Buckeye Partners have higher credit ratings (BBB+ or BBB-), making them more attractive for investors seeking simpler and more stable dividend stocks. The article suggests that investors looking to avoid the added complexity of ETE should consider these stand-alone MLPs instead.
